corrections.original: BERT set new records on 11 tasks, including GLUE 80.5 (arXiv 11 Oct 2018)
corrections.fix: The 11 Oct 2018 v1 reports GLUE 80.4 (+7.6). 80.5 (+7.7) is from the v2 revision of 24 May 2019. Give the version when citing the number.

corrections.original: ELMo (February 2018), the first of the big pretrained contextual models
corrections.fix: Not first: CoVe (arXiv 1 Aug 2017) and ULMFiT (arXiv 18 Jan 2018) predate it, and GPT-1 cites Dai & Le 2015 and ULMFiT. ELMo used bi-LSTMs (verified). Its NAACL 2018 honour is 'Outstanding Paper'; the 'best paper' and '27 Oct 2017 OpenReview' claims are unverified.

corrections.original: Anthropic's Olsson et al. (8 Mar 2022) identified induction heads
corrections.fix: Induction heads were first named and described in Elhage et al., 'A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits' (22 Dec 2021). Olsson et al. ('In our previous paper, we discovered ... induction heads') linked them to in-context learning. The phase-change bump, 'actual majority' and 'preliminary and indirect' quotes are verified.

corrections.original: Weeks/two weeks after submission, Kaiser emailed Gomez 'Generated Wikipedia Articles'
corrections.fix: The New Yorker says 'Two weeks later', meaning after the 3 a.m. late-sprint conversation, with Gomez back at school in Toronto. It does not tie this to the submission. The model was given two days to read 'a little less than half' of Wikipedia.

corrections.original: Per Parmar, they toasted 'with warm bubbly beside the dusty vehicle in the company parking lot'
corrections.fix: That phrase is Marche's narration. Parmar's only quoted words are 'Jakob had some old champagne in his car.' Do not present the narration as her words.

corrections.original: Gomez 'produced some diagrams for the paper' (Wired)
corrections.fix: Wired: Gomez 'produced the visualizations and diagrams for the paper'. Note that the paper's footnote credits Llion Jones with 'visualizations'.

corrections.original: Uszkoreit chose the name 'Transformers' partly because of his childhood toys
corrections.fix: Wired: 'They picked the name "transformers" from "day zero,"' where 'they' is Uszkoreit, Polosukhin and Vaswani, because the mechanism transforms information. 'Plus Uszkoreit had fond childhood memories' of the toys. Say the toys were an added reason for the trio's choice.

corrections.original: OpenAI released 355M (May 2019)
corrections.fix: At release (May 2019 update) OpenAI called it the '345M' model. It was relabelled 355M by the 20 Aug 2019 follow-up. The 774M (20 Aug) and 1.5B (5 Nov 2019) releases are verified.

corrections.original: The 'too dangerous to release' framing came from the Guardian headline, not OpenAI
corrections.fix: Verified: OpenAI's 14 Feb 2019 post never says 'too dangerous'. But the Guardian headline attributes the framing to the creators ('say creators'), and we cannot show the Guardian originated it. Brundage: 'distinguish what we said from what others said'. Say 'the press framed it as too dangerous to release'. The Anandkumar and Rao criticisms are verified verbatim.

corrections.original: Spring 2017: Shazeer overhears Vaswani and Parmar and joins
corrections.fix: Wired says only 'one day in 2017', while passing Kaiser's workspace in Building 1965. The season is not given.

corrections.original: Timeline lists Seq2Seq (10 Sep 2014) before Bahdanau (1 Sep 2014); Seq2Seq/GNMT dates marked not re-fetched
corrections.fix: Reordered. arXiv confirms 1 Sep 2014 (1409.0473), 10 Sep 2014 (1409.3215) and 26 Sep 2016 (1609.08144); all upgraded to primary.

corrections.original: By March 2024 all eight had left Google ... Shazeer was rehired by Google in August 2024 (2026 moves LEAD only)
corrections.fix: The March 2024 list and the Aug 2024 rehire are verified (Verge, 2 Aug 2024 US time). The claim is now incomplete: Shazeer, then Gemini co-lead, left Google for OpenAI on 17–18 Jun 2026 (Reuters, CNBC and Axios headlines). Upgraded from LEAD to VERIFIED-SECONDARY at headline level.

corrections.original: Wikipedia: Cohere acquired Aleph Alpha (24 Apr 2026)
corrections.fix: It is a merger: announced Apr 2026 (TechCrunch, 25 Apr 2026, 'Why Cohere is merging with Aleph Alpha') and the agreement was signed 16 Sep 2026 (PR Newswire, Reuters). Verified at headline level.

corrections.original: Parmar's reported move to Anthropic, late 2024: UNVERIFIED
corrections.fix: Multiple outlets reported it in Feb–Mar 2025 (Analytics India Magazine, 25 Feb 2025; Moneycontrol, 1 Mar 2025, 'Anthropic's Niki Parmar'). Headline-level only; the start date is unverified.

corrections.original: Vaswani PhD adviser David Chiang (Wikipedia LEAD)
corrections.fix: Wikipedia lists two doctoral advisers, David Chiang and Liang Huang (thesis 2014). Still a LEAD.

corrections.original: Figure 4: from 'its' the attention is 'very sharp', pointing at 'Law' and 'application'
corrections.fix: The caption says 'the attentions are very sharp for this word'. The targets 'Law'/'application' come from reading the figure, not from the caption text.

corrections.original: Big model dropout 0.3 (Table 3) presented without qualification
corrections.fix: The EN–FR big model used P_drop = 0.1 instead of 0.3 (§6.1). Base dropout 0.1 is confirmed.

corrections.original: Essential AI and Vaswani 'acqui-hired' by Nvidia (Jun 2026)
corrections.fix: Only Wikipedia, citing a blocked Axios page; no other outlet found. Do not state.

corrections.original: Jensen Huang hosted a GTC panel with seven of the eight authors on 20 Mar 2024
corrections.fix: A VentureBeat headline of 20 Mar 2024 supports that a GTC panel of the authors took place, but the article 404s. Who hosted it and how many attended remain unverified.

corrections.original: ELMo first appeared on OpenReview on 27 Oct 2017
corrections.fix: No source checked. Removed from the timeline; use the arXiv date of 15 Feb 2018.
